newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo Nobel down on mini-pill worries.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel down on mini-pill worries.

text.p: Shares in Dutch chemicals and pharmaceuticals group Akzo Nobel fell in Amsterdam on Friday on reports that a new study had firmed up the disputed link between third-generation contraceptive pills and thrombosis in users.
Akzo shares were down 7.00 guilders, 2.64 percent, to 258.00 at 0850 GMT in a generally lower market.
Akzo unit Organon is a leading producer of the low-dosage "mini-pills", which have been restricted in some European countries because of fears over blood clotting problems.
A Dutch newspaper on Friday reported a University of Maastricht study had shown the synthetic hormones in the pills did have a negative effect on the body's clotting system.
"Well it is definitely a worry for the market," one dealer said. "Last time the issue came up it looked like it wouldn't be so bad for Akzo, but who knows how to take this."
